sounds.intro: Italian is spelled almost exactly as it sounds. Vowels are pure and short, and every letter is pronounced.
rows: hold the sound a little longer

phrases.title: Formal and informal
phrases.note: tu (informal): friends, family, young people. Lei (formal, capital L): strangers, older people, work. With Lei the verb is the he/she form. Use Lei when unsure.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Italian drops subject pronouns most of the time, because the verb ending shows who is speaking.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Masculine -o → -i. Feminine -a → -e. Words in -e → -i. The article changes too: il → i, la → le, lo → gli.

grammar.title: Avere: to have
text: Avere is also used for age and feelings: ho sedici anni, ho fame, ho sete.

grammar.title: Regular verbs (present tense)
text: Three families: -are, -ere, -ire. Drop the ending, add the new one. Parlare (to speak):

grammar.title: Andare: to go
text: Going to do something soon: andare + a + infinitive. Vado a mangiare = I am going to eat.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Order: subject, verb, rest. Adjectives usually come after the noun and agree with it. You can drop the subject.
rows: add time or place at the end
ex: we live in a big house

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put non before the verb. Double negatives are normal: non ho niente.
Put non before the verb. Italian uses double negatives: non ho niente (I do not have anything).
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Yes or no question: same words as a statement, with a rising voice and a question mark. Or add "vero?" (right?).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: tu / tuo for friends. Lei / suo for strangers. Lei is not "she" here: it is the polite you, and the verb is in the he / she form.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: avere (or essere) + past participle: ho parlato, sono andato. Future: infinitive + -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal (tu): -are verbs end in -a (parla), -ere / -ire verbs in -i (scrivi). Negative tu: non + infinitive (non parlare). Formal (Lei): parli, scriva.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: potere (can), dovere (must), volere (want) + infinitive: posso nuotare, devo andare, voglio mangiare.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: in = in; su = on; a = at / to; sotto = under; accanto a = next to; vicino a = near; alle nove = at nine.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
il gatto è sotto il tavolo
eel GAHT-toh eh SOHT-toh eel TAH-voh-loh
the shop is next to the bank
il negozio è accanto alla banca
eel neh-GOH-tsee-oh eh ahk-KAHN-toh AHL-lah BAHN-kah
the park is near the station
il parco è vicino alla stazione
eel PAR-koh eh vee-CHEE-noh AHL-lah stah-tsee-OH-neh
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: più + adjective + di / che = more than (più grande di me). meno... di = less than. il più... = the most. migliore = better, peggiore = worse.
ex: grande, più grande, il più grande
GRAHN-deh pyoo GRAHN-deh eel pyoo GRAHN-deh
piccolo, più piccolo, il più piccolo
PEEK-koh-loh pyoo PEEK-koh-loh eel pyoo PEEK-koh-loh
lei è più alta di me
lay eh pyoo AHL-tah dee meh
Tashkent è più grande di Samarcanda
tahsh-KEHNT eh pyoo GRAHN-deh dee sah-mar-KAHN-dah
